      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "why storage write errors should be handled rather than immediately terminating the process",
      "quote": "Can you expand on why this is a problem? If there is a storage error, don't we have to crash anyways?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained that handling the exception allows reporting the error and clean shutdown rather than std::terminate",

      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5362874919",
      "status_by_quote": "Handling the exception lets the node report the storage error and run its normal shutdown cleanup."
    },

      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "find a code pattern or compiler/linter check to avoid exception-during-destruction issues wholesale rather than addressing them piecemeal",
      "quote": "It would be good to find a code pattern that avoids this class of problem wholesale. It doesn't seem a great use of human (or LLM) review time to spend on such issues one-by-one.",
